data.narrative:
Orchid is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Noor Siddiqui that has raised $16.5M to date. The target operates within Biotech & Health, a sector represented by 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here and forms the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised of $16M as a proxy for Series A value, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—standard for progression to the next financing stage—yields $33M. This method directly reflects typical venture capital pricing dynamics at the Series A juncture. Peer-median triangulation cannot be applied due to an insufficient narrow peer set; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none of the tightly filtered subsets (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) contain the minimum 3 datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring using the Biotech & Health P/S median of 6.2x across the three public tickers is not executable absent the target's revenue, which private companies rarely disclose.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $28M (low) to $38M (high), centered on a $33M median. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the lack of disclosed comparable transaction multiples for early-stage biotech within Orchid's specific sub-segment and the absence of revenue or clinical-stage data necessary for alternative valuation approaches.
